Goals: Monitor and recognize change in signs and symptoms.
Be able to react adequately to change in signs and symptoms.
Know how and when to contact a healthcare professional.
Recommended self-management actions: Provide individualized information to support self-management.
If increasing dyspnoea or oedema or a sudden unexpected weight gain of >2 kg in 3 days occurs, patients may increase their diuretic dose and/or alert their healthcare team.

Psychological issues - Goals: To be able to live a good life with HF.
To be able to seek help in case of psychological problems such as depressive symptoms, anxiety or low mood which may occur in the course of the HF trajectory.
To recognise that the carer or family members may be greatly affected and need to seek help.
Psychological issues - Recommendations: Regularly communicate information on disease, treatment options and self-care.
Regularly discuss the need for support.
Treat or refer to specialist for psychological support when necessary.
Family and informal caregivers - Goals: To be able to ask for support.
Family and informal caregivers - Recomme: Discuss the preference of caregiver/family involvement.
Involve patients and caregivers in a respectful way.

Key points: Physical conditioning by exercise training improves exercise tolerance and health-related quality of life (QOL) in patients with HF.
Clinical trials and meta-analyses in people with HFrEF show that exercise rehabilitation improves exercise capacity and QOL.
Meta-analyses also show reduced all-cause and HF hospitalizations, though uncertainty remains about effects on mortality.
Benefits on hospitalization are seen in those highly adherent to the exercise programme.
High-intensity interval training, in patients who are able and willing, may improve peak oxygen consumption (VO2).
Supervised exercise-based rehabilitation should be considered for those who are frail or have more severe disease or comorbidities.
